authority: Regional Transport Office (RTO) / Automated Testing Station (ATS)

description.en: A Vehicle Fitness Certificate is a mandatory certificate issued after inspection of a motor vehicle to certify that it meets the prescribed safety and emission standards. Under the Motor Vehicles Act, transport vehicles require fitness certification from the date of registration, while personal vehicles require it after 15 years from the date of first registration.

verifiedConditions.claim: The vehicle must be registered with an RTO in India and have a valid registration certificate (RC).
Transport vehicles (taxis, buses, trucks, auto-rickshaws, goods carriers) require a fitness certificate from the date of registration. The certificate must be renewed periodically.

unverifiedEligibility: Personal (non-transport) vehicles older than 15 years from the date of first registration require a fitness certificate for re-registration.
Vehicles modified or involved in major accidents may need an additional fitness inspection.
Some states have started requiring fitness testing at Automated Testing Stations (ATS) instead of manual RTO inspection.

requirements.claim: Application in Form 20 (Application for Certificate of Fitness) submitted online through the Vahan portal or at the RTO.
Original vehicle registration certificate (RC) or smart card RC.
Valid motor vehicle insurance certificate covering at least third-party liability.
Valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate from an authorized testing centre.
Proof of road tax payment (tax token or online receipt).
The vehicle must be physically presented for inspection at the RTO or Automated Testing Station on the scheduled date.

processInformation.claim: Submit the application in Form 20 online through the Vahan portal or at the RTO. Book an inspection appointment for the vehicle.

Present the vehicle for physical inspection at the designated RTO or Automated Testing Station. The inspection checks brakes, steering, headlights, indicators, horn, tyres, emissions, body condition, and safety equipment.
If the vehicle passes all inspection parameters, the fitness certificate is issued. If it fails, the owner is given time to rectify defects and present the vehicle for re-inspection.

output.claim: A Certificate of Fitness in Form 38 endorsed on the registration certificate, certifying the vehicle meets prescribed road-worthiness standards. For transport vehicles, the fitness certificate is valid for 2 years from the date of issue (1 year for vehicles older than 8 years).

fees.applicability: Vehicle fitness inspection fee (varies by vehicle type and state)
fees.claim: Fitness inspection fee ranges from Rs. 200 to Rs. 500 depending on the vehicle type (two-wheeler, four-wheeler, heavy vehicle) and the state.

processingTime.applicability: Vehicle fitness certificate from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: Fitness certificate is typically issued on the same day as the inspection if the vehicle passes. At Automated Testing Stations, the process is usually completed within a few hours. Delays may occur if the vehicle requires re-inspection.

sources.title: Vahan — National Vehicle Registration Portal
sources.publisher: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Vahan portal provides online services for vehicle fitness certificate applications, fee payment, and appointment scheduling for inspection.
claimsSupported: Online application through Vahan portal is available.
Form 20 is required for fitness certificate application.
RC, insurance, PUC, and tax receipt are required documents.
sources.uncertainty: Some states may still use manual inspection processes. ATS rollout is ongoing across states.

sources.title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 56 (Certificate of Fitness)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Section 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act provides for the certificate of fitness for transport vehicles. A transport vehicle cannot be used in a public place unless it holds a valid fitness certificate.
claimsSupported: Transport vehicles require fitness certificate from date of registration.
Fitness certificate validity is 2 years (1 year for vehicles over 8 years old).
Physical inspection of the vehicle is mandatory.
sources.uncertainty: The 2019 amendment introduced provisions for Automated Testing Stations which are being implemented gradually.

limitations: Fee structure and inspection procedures vary by state and whether the state has Automated Testing Stations.
The record primarily covers transport vehicles. Personal vehicle fitness testing after 15 years is a newer requirement.
Re-inspection rules and timelines for vehicles that fail initial inspection vary by RTO.
The record does not cover fitness certification for modified vehicles or imported vehicles.
ATS availability and standards may differ from state to state.

review.reviewReason: Core fitness certificate process verified from Motor Vehicles Act and Parivahan portal. State-wise ATS implementation status needs tracking.
nextReviewTrigger: Full rollout of Automated Testing Stations nationwide.
Changes to fitness certificate validity periods.
